title: RFC 8439 ChaCha20 4-way parallel 20-round keystream block (256 bytes)

target_block_header.x86_64: for x86_64 needs avx needs avx512 { ... }

contract_header:
use spec = "r6y26tckd64yc2ryvfe6ekd6tcepzrjmksdufiqqx6xmqvoix2ta"  // chacha20_4way_spec.ode

fn chacha20_4way(out: 256 bytes, st: 256 bytes)
    requires disjoint(out, st, 1)
    ensures out = bytes_of(spec.chacha20_4way(words(st)))
    stack 256
task_summary: Implement `chacha20_4way(out, st)`, which computes four independent 64-byte RFC 8439 ChaCha20 20-round keystream blocks from the four contiguous 16-word initial states in `st[0..63]` (`256 bytes`) and writes the four 16-word keystream blocks to `out[0..63]` (`256 bytes`), all as little-endian 32-bit unsigned words (`words(st)` / `bytes_of(...)`). Both 128-bit SIMD (`xmm0..xmm15` with `vpaddd`, `vpxord`, `vprord`, `vpshufd`, `vmovdqu` on x86-64; NEON `v0..v31` with `add.4s`, `eor.16b`, `rev32.8h`, `shl.4s`, `ushr.4s`, `orr.16b`, `ext.16b` on AArch64) and 512-bit AVX-512 (`zmm0..zmm31` with `vpaddd`, `vpxord`, `vprord`, `vpunpck*`, `vmovdqu32` on x86-64) are available in the instruction tables. Your goal is BOTH full verification (`shown`) AND maximum throughput (lowest cycles per 256-byte call and `cyc/B`).
opt_goal: reduce total cycles per 256-byte call (and `cyc/B`) toward the vector execution-port floor (e.g., by interleaving all 4 blocks across independent vector registers to hide ARX rotate/add latency, or using 512-bit AVX-512 `zmm` registers with 4-way transpose on x86-64) while keeping verification fast (`shown`) and stack accesses 16-byte/64-byte aligned
